title: Critical Skills Employment Permit in Ireland: Eligible Tech and Pharma Occupations

runs.t: Ireland’s Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) is designed to attract highly skilled workers in occupations considered important to the economy and in shortage. For international graduates, the key question is not simply whether a job is in technology or pharmaceuticals. Eligibility depends on the exact occupation and specialism, the salary threshold, the applicant’s qualifications and a qualifying job offer.

Check the current Critical Skills Occupations List using the actual duties and SOC occupational classification—not just the job title. From 2026, the standard minimum annual remuneration is €40,904 for qualifying listed occupations requiring a relevant degree; a lower threshold of €36,848 applies to qualifying recent graduates under the stated conditions. Other eligible occupations may use the higher €68,911 threshold, subject to exclusions and rules.

The CSEP is an employment permit for eligible highly skilled roles. It is intended to attract workers in strategically important occupations and support longer-term employment in Ireland. A qualifying offer must generally be for at least two years from a bona fide employer based and trading in Ireland. The employer and role must meet the legal requirements.

runs.t: Thresholds are applied at the time of application and may be revised. Salary components and exclusions are defined by DETE; do not use total compensation or bonuses as a substitute for the qualifying remuneration rules.

sections.title: Tech roles: check the occupational specialism

runs.t: The current Critical Skills Occupations List includes selected ICT occupations such as IT specialist managers, IT project and programme managers, IT business analysts, architects and systems designers, programmers and software development professionals, web design and development professionals, and other ICT professionals. The list may specify particular skills within a broad occupational group.

A graduate with a master’s in data science, computer science or information systems should not assume that every data analyst, business analyst, product role or AI-related job qualifies. The actual duties, seniority, specialist skills, SOC classification and employer’s job description matter.

The current list includes selected health and scientific occupations, including pharmacists and industrial pharmacists, medical scientists and other specified health professionals. Some engineering and process roles relevant to high-technology manufacturing, quality control, validation, regulation, chemical processing and automation may also be listed when the exact specialism meets the stated criteria.

A role in a pharmaceutical company is not automatically a Critical Skills occupation. For example, a general administration, sales, production support or laboratory assistant job may not meet the CSEP criteria merely because the employer operates in the pharma sector.
Obtain the full job description, including daily duties, required skills, seniority and reporting line.
Identify the most appropriate SOC occupational code based on the work actually performed.
Search the current Critical Skills Occupations List and read the specific skills/specialism wording.
Check whether the role is on the Ineligible List for Employment Permits.
Confirm the minimum salary threshold, qualifying remuneration components and any recent-graduate concession.
Confirm that the offer is for at least two years and that the employer meets the bona fide employer conditions.
Check qualification, experience and any professional registration requirements.
Ensure the application is submitted at least 12 weeks before the proposed employment start date, as advised by DETE.

sections.title: What students should do before choosing a course

runs.t: Look at current employer demand and job descriptions—not only broad sector growth headlines.
Compare course modules with the specialist skills in current eligible occupation entries.
Check whether professional registration is required for regulated roles.
Build practical experience through projects, internships and relevant work experience.
Understand that the permit is employer- and role-specific; it is not granted simply because a student has an Irish qualification.
Review the list again close to graduation because occupations and thresholds can change.

faq.q: Is data science on Ireland’s Critical Skills list?

runs.t: Some ICT and analytical occupations may qualify depending on the actual duties and occupational classification. A degree title such as Data Science does not itself establish eligibility.

faq.q: Are all pharma jobs eligible for a CSEP?

runs.t: No. The role must match an eligible occupation or another qualifying category and meet salary, employer and qualification conditions.

faq.q: What is the 2026 CSEP salary threshold?

runs.t: The standard threshold for a qualifying listed occupation with a relevant degree is €40,904; a qualifying recent graduate threshold is €36,848. Other eligible occupations may require more than €68,911.
No. It may provide a route to apply for Stamp 4 after the required period and subject to the conditions then in force.

faq.q: How early should an employment permit be filed?

runs.t: DETE says an application should be received at least 12 weeks before the proposed employment start date.
